problem_type: Recovery routing follows mutable selection instead of submitted job identity
symptom: Retrieve again can query the wrong provider or model after a node selection changes.
direct_cause: buildRecoverPayload reads selectedVendor and selectedModelKey despite an existing run.attempt snapshot.
class_root: Recovery query routing does not honor immutable submission identity at its shared payload boundary.
affected_population: Any non-production canvas task with a saved attempt and changed provider/model selection
Imported ComfyUI candidate workflows and cloud providers
entry_points: Production-owned recovery delegates to durable Production Run
internal_only_reason: This invariant is controlled by Nomi saved run records and internal task routing, not a third-party protocol.
invariants: When a run has a submitted provider/model snapshot, retrieve using that snapshot.
Do not attach a newly selected model mode to an earlier model task.
Production Run ownership and project identity checks remain intact.
Persist the exact built request task kind and mode before transport submission; recovery must use this snapshot despite later reference/mode edits.

door_reduction.why_not: Recovery consumption, executor forwarding, provider-bound submission and schema parsing are separate lifecycle boundaries; each is necessary and now shares one persisted query snapshot rather than independent routing guesses.

generality_proof: All legacy canvas recovery queries pass through buildRecoverPayload. Provider-independent regression cases cover cloud and imported ComfyUI identities; production-owned jobs already use durable run retrieval.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Existing registered generation gateway awaits persistence of the exact built request routing before any provider submission. Recovery reads that same stored identity.

Existing registered run-outcome writer owns original-project identity delivery. Its local persistSubmittedRunAttempt helper retains receipt fields, flushes the existing save owner and verifies the bound disk receipt; no second run writer is introduced.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Every legacy task query consumes buildRecoverPayload.
Production-owned nodes delegate to durable run retrieval before the legacy payload path.

recurrence.reason: Any later selection change can affect an earlier task across providers and future runs.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs buildRecoverPayload: one production entry, src/electron 3063 files searched.
rg attempt.vendorKey and attempt?.vendorKey in runner: nodeModelHealth already reads saved attempt identity.
Checked recoverNodeResult production dispatch before legacy recovery.

prevention.invariant: Saved run routing takes precedence over mutable next-run selection.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing task/vendor retains existing missing-task error; project mismatch remains refused.
prevention.strategy: Persist exact built request routing through the existing run-started delivery before submission; consume this immutable query snapshot at the recovery boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed unconditional selected-vendor/model routing when an immutable attempt exists; no parallel recovery engine added.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency controls which persisted identity is selected for the query.

migration: New tasks persist query kind/mode from the final built request before submission. Historical records remain readable and preserve prior best-effort inference only when no exact query snapshot exists; missing historical inputs are not fabricated.
residual_risks: Live UI retrieval and restart into this isolated build remain unverified.
Legacy records without an attempt cannot recover unavailable historical identity.
Historical records lacking an exact query snapshot still depend on existing legacy reference/mode inference; original absent inputs cannot be guessed.

Single-submit characterization fixtures now register the existing durable save owner and preserve workspace identity; no production persistence check was relaxed. The missing-owner failure was reproduced in single-submit-diagnostic.log.
